quote.text: Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.
quote.author: Warren Buffett, 2008 Berkshire Hathaway letter, after Benjamin Graham

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 7 · Umbrellas & Rain Kit
stories.headline: The Object You Will Lose in a Taxi, Made to Outlive the Taxi
stories.dek: In a city of hard sun and sudden squalls, the umbrella is the most-used, least-considered thing you own. The quality is all in the frame — and the honest answer is that the storm umbrella and the heirloom are two different tools.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · The Invitation — Mechanical Keyboards
stories.headline: Grown Adults Are Chasing a Sound Called "Thock." The Keyboard Is the Instrument.
stories.dek: There is a fork most people never notice they've reached: on one side the sealed gaming keyboard you replace when it dies, on the other a thing you build from chosen parts and tune for how it sounds. The enthusiast world lives entirely on the second side.

stories.headline: A Pass Gets Dearer, Europe's Borders Get Biometric, and Changi Gets a Terminal for One
stories.dek: What actually changed on the departures board since the last weekend: the JR Pass rises for the first time in three years, Europe's fingerprint borders are live while its travel permit slips again, and a private terminal breaks ground at Changi.

stories.headline: The Truce Broke Two Days Early, and the Tariff Wall Went Back Up
stories.dek: A deadline meant to hold to Monday collapsed on Friday. Washington put fifty-per-cent tariffs on twenty billion dollars of Canadian goods; Ottawa called the terms "unfair, uneconomic," walked out, and promised to match them dollar for dollar from 8 September.

stories.headline: The Headlines Say Runaway. The Index Says Cooling.
stories.dek: A record run of million-dollar flats is doing all the shouting. Underneath it, the broad HDB resale market has quietly fallen for two quarters straight — the first back-to-back dip since 2019, and the number that actually touches a mid-forties upgrader.

stories.headline: Nobody Has to Import the Banned Chip. They Just Rent It.
stories.dek: Washington's chip controls govern the physical transfer of hardware — not remote access to it. So the fix Chinese labs found was to stop shipping chips and start renting the compute, in data centres a plane ride away. The law is now scrambling to catch a loophole it wrote into itself.

stories.headline: Insta360 Put a One-Inch Sensor in a 360 Camera. Then Shipped a Buggy App With It.
stories.dek: The X6 is the best-looking 360 footage the reviewers have tested — dual one-inch-equivalent sensors, 8K at fifty frames, in-camera Dolby Vision. It is also the most expensive small 360 camera you can buy, and the app that edits it keeps crashing.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Driver's Chronograph
stories.headline: Eleven Thousand Euros, a Mountain Pass, and a Movement Chopard Didn't Make
stories.dek: The 2026 Mille Miglia Raticosa is the prettiest rendition of Chopard's racing chronograph in years — a warm eggshell dial, a steering-wheel crown, a nod to a hairpin on the route. It also asks haute-horlogerie money for an outsourced calibre, and the purists have noticed.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Weekend Watch & Listen
stories.headline: A Six-Year Silence Ends, a Road With No Exit, and the Film Nobody Was Allowed to See
stories.dek: Phoebe Bridgers returns to a wall of acclaim and one honest dissent; a ninety-four-per-cent horror sleeper opens wide; and the cartoon lawsuit a studio tried to bury for a tax write-off arrives, vindicated.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Study That Surprised Itself
stories.headline: A Screen-Time Study Went Looking for Harm. It Found the Opposite.
stories.dek: An eight-year Finnish cohort set out to document what screens do to a developing brain, and the association ran the other way. The lesson for a Secondary One household is not "more is fine" — it is that the stopwatch was always the wrong instrument.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Debasement Bid
stories.headline: The Treasury Threw Four Billion at the Long Bond. It Didn't Hold.
stories.dek: Last weekend's setup was a guidance-less Fed and a Treasury buying its own long end. The delta this week: the buyback rally fizzled, the minutes showed a hike back on the table, and bitcoin ran up a fifth in seven days on the same bid that lifts gold.

stories.headline: Two Hours of Lifting a Week Buys the Longevity. The Third Hour Doesn't.
stories.dek: A 147,000-person analysis found the strength-training sweet spot — and it is smaller than the optimizer crowd wants to hear. Past about two hours a week the mortality benefit plateaus; the real multiplier is pairing it with the aerobic base.

stories.kicker: The Diary · The Stadium Autumn, and a Sprint
stories.headline: A Wall of Stadium Nights, and Singapore's First Formula One Sprint Weekend
The Morning After Hoesik
stories.dek: Everyone will eventually write "Koreans quit soju." The story underneath is stranger and more important: a sober, live-alone generation is rebuilding belonging from scratch — opt-in, scheduled, sober, and governed by an explicit rule that no one is allowed to date.
